title: Why Are Bubbles Always Round?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why are floating bubbles always round?
Blow through a square wand, and the bubble still comes out round.
A soap film is pulled tight by surface tension. It always shrinks itself as small as it can.
But the air trapped inside pushes back.
So the film settles on the shape that holds that air with the least surface.
That shape is a sphere. A cube holding the same air would need about a quarter more film.
Any bulge costs extra film, so the film pulls it back, and the wobbles fade away.
The wand shapes the start. Physics shapes the bubble.
